target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures report Consumer Banking net income and the primary drivers of the change (revenue, provision for credit losses, noninterest expense). 2023 D066 cites a decrease of $923m to $11.6B. 2024 D066 cites a decrease of $834m to $10.8B. They share the same specific subject of Net Income results.

2023 D066 covers the full Consumer Banking Results including Net Income, Provision for Credit Losses, and Noninterest Expense. In 2024, this content was split: D066 covers Net Income/Revenue components, while D067 covers Provision and Noninterest Expense. Therefore, the single 2023 disclosure corresponds to both 2024 disclosures covering the split financial results.

Both disclosures report Noninterest expense for the Consumer Banking segment. D076 (2024) reports $13.7 billion with a $349 million increase driven by people, technology, and operations. D066 (2023) reports $21.4 billion with a $1.3 billion increase driven by investments in people and technology, litigation, and FDIC expense. Both are specific Consumer Banking expense disclosures.
